subject.title: Agent lane lacks first-class scoped node exec path and stale nodes can hang or fail roughly

question: Should Codex app-server sessions expose a separate remote-node exec tool when the effective exec host remains local/auto, and what exact stale-node failure contract should that tool return?
rationale: Automation should not choose this boundary because it broadens model-visible remote shell access while keeping local Codex native execution active in the same lane.

options.title: Approve explicit mixed-session node exec
options.body: Expose pinned `node_exec`/`node_process` beside native local Codex tools, reuse the existing approval path, and add structured retryable node-unavailable results.

options.title: Require whole-session host=node
options.body: Keep the current model where remote shell is available only when the session's effective exec host is `node`, and document mixed local-plus-node execution as unsupported.

options.title: Defer to broader node-tool design
options.body: Route this through node-hosted tool/capability work instead of adding a generic shell surface now.

recommendation.title: Approve explicit mixed-session node exec
recommendation.body: Expose pinned `node_exec`/`node_process` beside native local Codex tools, reuse the existing approval path, and add structured retryable node-unavailable results.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc authored and recently maintained the current Codex `node_exec` implementation that this decision would extend or constrain.
